verses.text: At that time Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goiim
went to war against Bera king of Sodom, Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, Shemeber king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela, also called Zoar.
All of these kings joined forces in the Valley of Siddim, which is now the Salt Sea.
For 12 years they had served Chedorlaomer, but in the thirteenth year they rebelled.
In the fourteenth year, Chedorlaomer and the kings with him came and defeated the Rephaim at Ashteroth Karnaim, the Zuzim at Ham, and the Emim at Shaveh Kiriathaim,
as well as the Horites in the mountains of Seir, as far as El Paran near the wilderness.
On their way back, they came to En Mishpat, also called Kadesh, and defeated the whole territory of the Amalekites and the Amorites living in Hazazon Tamar.
Then the kings of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, Zeboiim, and Bela (that is, Zoar) marched out and lined up for battle in the Valley of Siddim
against Chedorlaomer king of Elam, Tidal king of Goiim, Amraphel king of Shinar, and Arioch king of Ellasar—four kings against five.
The Valley of Siddim was full of tar pits. As the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled, some fell into them, while the rest escaped to the hills.
The enemy took all the goods and food from Sodom and Gomorrah, then left.
They also took Lot, Abram's nephew, who was living in Sodom, along with his possessions, and went away.
One man who escaped came and told Abram the Hebrew. Abram was living by the oaks of Mamre the Amorite, who was the brother of Eshcol and Aner. They were Abram's allies.
When Abram heard that his relative had been captured, he called out the 318 trained men born in his household and chased the enemy as far as Dan.
That night Abram divided his men and attacked them. He pursued them as far as Hobah, on the left side of Damascus.
He brought back all the goods, his relative Lot and Lot's possessions, the women, and the other people.
After Abram returned from defeating Chedorlaomer and the kings with him, the king of Sodom came out to meet him in the Valley of Shaveh, also called the King's Valley.
Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine. He was a priest of God Most High.
He blessed Abram and said, "May Abram be blessed by God Most High, the Maker of heaven and earth.
Blessed be God Most High, who handed your enemies over to you." Then Abram gave Melchizedek a tenth of everything.
The king of Sodom said to Abram, "Give me the people, and keep the goods for yourself."
Abram replied to the king of Sodom, "I have raised my hand in an oath to Yahweh, God Most High, Maker of heaven and earth.
I will not take even a thread, a sandal strap, or anything else that belongs to you. Then you couldn't say, 'I made Abram rich.'
I'll take nothing for myself except what the young men have already eaten and the share for the men who came with me—Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre. Let them take their share."
